title: langaccess
description: langaccess classifies the language access a website provides. Given an address, it renders the site in a headless browser and fetches the same address again with no scripts run. For each language it finds, it records whether the text is the site's own writing or the output of a translation widget. A widget rewrites the page in the browser and leaves the served document unchanged, so the two readings differ where a widget is at work. Each result names the class, the languages, the URL and quoted text that decided it, the codebook rules applied, a read-quality record and the build that produced it. A verdict can be checked from that record without repeating the crawl. The classification describes the site's text and makes no claim about service quality. Version 0.2.0 reads eleven more languages from their own function words and scripts, refuses addresses that are not web addresses, distinguishes a domain that no longer resolves from a page that could not be read, names the cause of every failed read, and judges a live audit and a stored capture with one reader. Agreement with a 1,992-address gold dataset is reported in LIMITATIONS.md.

Cite the version that produced your readings: a verdict is the output of one rule set, so a citation that does not name the version has not said which instrument produced its numbers.
